input.summary:
parts/room-29.mjs ("P3 rear bedroom") now builds with 0 refused and 0 off-palette writes: 6 placed (2 barrels, chest, flower pot, candle, lantern), bed() unchanged.
The oak_fence nightstand at (58,6,20) and its lantern at (58,7,20) were dropped because the roof owns those cells; the lantern moved to (59,7,18) standing on the middle barrel.
make.sh now saves build.nbt with 11527 cells; the part's line in parts-report.json reads refused 0, offPalette [].
left: Roof intrusion, not this part: the gambrel's lower slope takes the back-west corner of this room (deepslate_tiles at 58,6,20 and deepslate_tile_stairs at 58,7,20). The same kind of clash refuses writes in P3 upper hall, P3 dormer bedroom and P3 west bedroom. Fix the roof part, not these rooms.

bed(g, [59,6,20], 'east') returns false silently when a cell is taken; I did not check its return value. The plan shows cells 59,60 at z20 as occupied, but I did not confirm both bed halves are bed blocks.
The lantern's light level was not checked with mcd light; the room is only 6 blocks of light sources in a 3x3 floor.

waste.what: Diagnosing each refusal by hand: reading parts-report.json, then reading the plan grid to work out which cells were roof and which were free, and choosing a lantern cell that keeps the entry lane clear.
waste.cost: About 4 tool calls, 2 edits and 1 rebuild. I reasoned through the free cells one at a time.
waste.tool: mcd plan could mark each 'o' cell with the part that owns it (roof, shell, room) and list the free cells that are supported and off the entry lane. A refusal line could also name the owning part.

waste.what: Checking that the bed was placed. bed() returns false silently on a taken cell, and the part's placed count does not include the bed.
waste.cost: One extra plan run, and the bed check was inferred from the plan's 'o' marks rather than confirmed.
waste.tool: bed() or the parts report could record its success in placed/refused. The report could list the bed separately.

waste.what: Working out that the nightstand cell is in the roof: the plan's floor label says y=6, while plan.md puts the upper floor block at y5 with feet at y6.
waste.cost: A few reasoning steps against plan.md, with no tool check.
waste.tool: mcd plan could print the floor block layer and the feet layer separately, so room parts do not read the floor label as the feet level.

companions.task: Look at the gambrel's lower slope where it meets the back-west corner (x58, z20, y6..7) and at the upper hall, dormer bedroom and west bedroom clashes. Decide whether to raise or step the roof there or to accept the headroom loss, before any room part is rebuilt.
